title: Hyperbolic dynamics and thermodynamic formalism
summary: Bowen's uniqueness criterion under weak specification for homeomorphisms and flows, on ClassicalErgodicTheory's pressure, variational principles and equilibrium states; hyperbolic sets, invariant manifolds and local product structure; Bowen's theorem, the Bowen-Ruelle theorem, Bowen-Margulis measures and the SRB theorem for hyperbolic attractors of flows generated by C^2 vector fields (Lebesgue-almost every point of the basin is generic), in particular for transitive C^2 Anosov flows.

targets.name: Dynamics.bowenBall
targets.statement: For a map T of a pseudometric space, d_n(x,y) = max_{0<=k<n} d(T^k x, T^k y) (0 for n = 0) and, for eps > 0, B_n(x,eps) is the open d_n-ball; for a flow g and real t >= 0, d_t(x,y) = sup_{0<=s<=t} d(g^s x, g^s y) (so d_0 = d) and B_t(x,eps) is the open d_t-ball.
hypotheses: T : X -> X, or g : Flow R X

locator.where: lines 163-164 (map separation, k in [0,n]) and lines 99-101 (closed flow balls); ClimenhagaThompson2016 lines 175-177

api.name: bowenBall_eq_ball_dynEntourage
api.statement: For eps > 0, B_n(x,eps) is the ball at x of Dynamics.dynEntourage T {d < eps} n; at eps = 0 the metric ball is empty while the entourage ball at n = 0 is univ.

api.name: bowenBall_zero
api.statement: For eps > 0, the map ball B_0(x,eps) = univ and B_1(x,eps) = ball x eps; the flow ball B_0(x,eps) is ball x eps.

api.name: bowenBall_antitone
api.statement: B_{n+1}(x,eps) is contained in B_n(x,eps); the flow balls B_t(x,eps) decrease as t increases; all balls increase with eps.

api.name: mapsTo_bowenBall
api.statement: T maps B_{n+1}(x,eps) into B_n(Tx,eps); a semiconjugacy h, Lipschitz with a constant L > 0, maps B^S_n(x,eps) into B^T_n(hx, L eps).

api.name: flow_bowenBall_comparison
api.statement: For t > 0, n >= 1 on a compact metric space, B_{nt}(x,eps) is contained in the g^t-ball B_n(x,eps), and the g^t-ball B_n(x,delta) is contained in B_{nt}(x,eps) when d(y,z) < delta implies d(g^s y, g^s z) < eps for s in [0,t]; the second containment fails at n = 0.

api.name: gammaSet_isClosed
api.statement: For a homeomorphism and eps > 0, Gamma_eps(x) = {y : d(T^k x, T^k y) <= eps for all k in Z} is the intersection over n >= 0 of T^n(closed B_{2n+1}(T^{-n} x, eps)), whose window is [-n, n]; it is closed, and compact when X is compact. For a flow, Gamma_eps(x) = {y : d(g^t x, g^t y) <= eps for all real t} (ClimenhagaThompson2016 lines 355-358), closed and compact in the same way.

tests.name: rotation_ball
tests.statement: For a rotation of R/Z, B_n(x,eps) is the eps-ball for every n >= 1.

tests.name: doubling_ball
tests.statement: For the doubling map and eps = 1/8, B_n(0,1/8) is the arc of half-width 2^(-n-2): 1/8 at n = 1, 1/16 at n = 2.

tests.name: ball_zero_univ
tests.statement: At n = 0 the Bowen ball is the whole space, matching coverMincard at time zero equal to 1 on a nonempty set.

tests.name: gamma_window
tests.statement: Two-shift, y with its only 1 at coordinate -1: d(T^k 0, T^k y) = 2^(-k-1) for k >= 0 but d(T^-1 0, T^-1 y) = 1, so y is not in Gamma_{1/2}(0); T(closed B_3(T^-1 0,1/2)) excludes y, while T^-n(closed B_{2n+1}(T^n 0,1/2)) tests times n..3n and contains y.

tests.name: gamma_rationals
tests.statement: Identity of Q: Gamma_1(0) = [-1,1] cap Q is closed and not compact; for the identity of R, [-1,1] is compact and is no counterexample.

tests.name: constant_map_radius
tests.statement: Constant map of a two-point space, L = 0, n = 1, eps = 1: the image point is not in the empty ball B_1(pt,0) but is in B_1(pt,1).

tests.name: flow_ball_n_zero
tests.statement: Unit-speed rotation of R/Z, t = 1, eps = 1/4: the time-one ball B_0(x,delta) is the circle, the flow ball B_0(x,1/4) is an arc; the converse containment needs n >= 1.

targets.name: Dynamics.IsEntropyExpansive
targets.statement: A uniformly continuous map T of a compact metric space is entropy-expansive at scale eps > 0 when coverEntropy T Phi_eps(x) = 0 for every x, Phi_eps(x) the points whose forward orbit stays within eps of that of x (two-sided Gamma_eps for homeomorphisms); such a map has coverEntropy T univ = coverEntropyEntourage T univ {d <= eps} < oo. Expansive homeomorphisms are ClassicalErgodicTheory's (5.3).

api.name: entropyExpansive_of_expansive
api.statement: An expansive homeomorphism with constant c (ClassicalErgodicTheory 5.3) is entropy-expansive at every scale eps < c, since Gamma_eps(x) = {x}.

api.name: finite_periodic_of_expansive
api.statement: An expansive homeomorphism of a compact metric space has finitely many points of each period: Fix(T^n) is (n, c)-separated.

api.name: entropyExpansive_mono
api.statement: Entropy-expansiveness at scale eps passes to smaller scales and to T^k, k >= 1, at a smaller scale.

tests.name: identity_interval
tests.statement: The identity of [0,1] is entropy-expansive at every scale but not expansive: finite entropy holds, finiteness of periodic points needs expansivity.

tests.name: full_shift_scale
tests.statement: Full two-shift, d = 2^(-N): expansive with c = 1/2, entropy-expansive at 1/4; {d <= 1/4}-closeness for T^0..T^(n-1) fixes coordinates -1..n, covers of size 2^(n+2), entropy log 2.

tests.name: shrinking_shifts
tests.statement: One-point compactification of full shifts on 2^m symbols scaled to diameter 2^(-m) at distance 2^(-m) from the added fixed point: Phi_eps(oo) contains pieces of entropy m log 2 for all large m, not entropy-expansive at any scale, entropy oo.

targets.name: Flow.expansive_gamma_subset_orbitSegment
targets.statement: For a Bowen-Walters expansive flow (ClassicalErgodicTheory IsExpansiveFlow, 8.5) on a compact metric space: for every eta > 0 some eps > 0 has Gamma_eps(x) in g^{[-eta,eta]} x for all x; fixed points are isolated; every time-t map, t != 0, is entropy-expansive at scale eps for d_|t| and every invariant measure is almost expansive; expansivity is preserved by reversal and rescaling g(at), a > 0.

locator.where: lines 355-366, 371-375, 380-381; Proposition 3.3, lines 513-530; BowenEntropyExpansive1972 Example 1.6, lines 117-133; BowenWalters1972

tests.name: periodic_orbit_expansive
tests.statement: The flow on a periodic orbit is expansive.

tests.name: linear_irrational_not
tests.statement: The irrational linear flow on the 2-torus is not expansive; Gamma_eps(x) contains a transverse segment.

tests.name: identity_flow
tests.statement: The identity flow of the circle is not expansive; of a finite set it is.

targets.name: Flow.IsTopologicallyMixing
targets.statement: A continuous flow is topologically mixing if for nonempty open U, V there is t0 with g^t U meeting V for all t >= t0; topological mixing of maps is ClassicalErgodicTheory's IsTopologicallyMixing (5.2).

api.name: mixing_transitive
api.statement: Mixing of maps and flows implies transitivity in forward time: AddAction.IsTopologicallyTransitive for Flow.fromIter of a map and for Flow.restrictNonneg of a flow; hence the weaker signed-time predicate.

api.name: mixing_iterate
api.statement: Mixing is conjugacy invariant and passes to factors; a homeomorphism is mixing iff some (every) power is mixing.

api.name: flow_mixing_iff_time
api.statement: A flow is mixing iff one (every) time-t map, t > 0, is mixing.

tests.name: periodic_orbit_not_mixing
tests.statement: The flow on a periodic orbit of period p is transitive, not mixing (g^t U misses U for t near p/2 + pZ); its time-p map is the identity.

tests.name: linear_irrational_not_mixing
tests.statement: The irrational linear flow on the 2-torus is minimal, not mixing.

tests.name: suspension_not_mixing
tests.statement: The constant-roof suspension of a homeomorphism of a nonempty compact metric space is not mixing; on the empty space mixing holds vacuously.

targets.name: Dynamics.HasWeakSpecification
targets.statement: Weak specification: for every delta > 0 there is tau such that any finite family of orbit segments is delta-shadowed by one orbit with gluing times at most tau (maps and flows); no periodic shadowing point is required.
hypotheses: T homeomorphism, or g continuous flow

api.name: strong_imp_weak
api.statement: Strong specification implies weak specification; ClassicalErgodicTheory's specification with periodic shadowing (HasSpecification 8.4, HasFlowSpecification 8.5) implies it, with all gluing times equal and at most M.

api.name: weak_imp_transitive
api.statement: Weak specification of a nonempty system implies transitivity in forward time (exists n >= 0, resp. t >= 0, with T^n U meeting V); the monotone shift, transitive only in signed time, has no weak specification.

api.name: weakSpec_conj
api.statement: Invariant under topological conjugacy of compact systems.

api.name: tail_spec
api.statement: For flows, tail specification at all scales gives the tail property used by ClimenhagaThompson2016 Lemma 2.10.

tests.name: swap_weak_not_strong
tests.statement: The swap of two points has weak specification with tau = 1 but no strong specification.

tests.name: suspension_not_periodic_spec
tests.statement: The roof-one suspension of the full two-shift has weak specification but not HasFlowSpecification: integer periods, and for p = n + 1/2, eps < 1/2 no |tau| <= eps makes p + tau a period; the swap of two points has weak specification and no periodic shadowing for odd p.

tests.name: full_shift_strong
tests.statement: The full shift has strong specification with gap about 2m at scale 2^(-m).

tests.name: disjoint_union_nonexample
tests.statement: A disjoint union of two full shifts has no weak specification.

targets.name: Flow.upperSemicontinuous_measureEntropy_of_expansive
targets.statement: For a Bowen-Walters expansive flow on a compact metric space there is eps > 0 with h_mu(g^1) = h_mu(g^1, xi) for every mu in M(g^1) and every finite partition xi of d_1-diameter < eps (ergodic case by ClimenhagaThompson2016 Theorem 3.2; general case by ArithmeticDynamics 2.7's ergodic decomposition with g_xi(x) = h_{mu_x}(g^1, xi)); mu -> h_mu(g^1) is upper semicontinuous on M(g^1), hence on M(g).

locator.where: Theorem 3.2 and Propositions 3.3-3.4, lines 504-535; BowenEntropyExpansive1972 Example 1.6

tests.name: periodic_orbit
tests.statement: Period-1 orbit: g^1 is the identity of the orbit, all entropies and rates 0; M(g) is one measure.

tests.name: suspension_log2
tests.statement: Product measure on the roof-one suspension of the two-shift: h(g^1) = log 2 by a small partition; the trivial partition gives 0, so the diameter hypothesis is needed.

tests.name: irrational_linear
tests.statement: The irrational linear flow is not expansive; all entropies are 0.

layers.title: Time-t maps and rescaling of flows

targets.name: Flow.isEquilibriumState_timeChange
targets.statement: For t > 0: topologicalPressure (g t) F_t = t flowTopologicalPressure g F (equivalently P_{g_a}(aF) = a P_g(F)); for mu in M(g), mu in ES_g(F) iff mu is an equilibrium state of F_t for g^t (t = 1 is ClassicalErgodicTheory 8.1); ES_{g_a}(aF) = ES_g(F); F' = F + c + L_g psi gives P' = P + c and ES' = ES (ClassicalErgodicTheory 8.5); when g is a C^1 flow on a manifold every C^1 psi qualifies with L_g psi = d psi(X).
hypotheses: psi continuous, differentiable along g with continuous derivative

tests.name: rescale_pressure
tests.statement: For g'(t) = g(2t), P_{g'}(2F) = 2 P_g(F); using F instead gives 2 P_g(F/2), different for nonconstant F.

tests.name: coboundary_integral
tests.statement: On a periodic orbit the integral of L_g psi over a period is 0.

tests.name: suspension_shift
tests.statement: F = 1 and 1 + L_g psi have the same equilibrium state, pressure log 2 + 1.

tests.name: invariance_needed
tests.statement: On a period-1 orbit point masses are equilibrium states of F_1 for g^1 but not in M(g).

tests.name: continuous_flow_c1_nonexample
tests.statement: Rotation of R/Z: psi = sin(2 pi s) has L_g psi = 2 pi cos(2 pi s); for the rotation conjugated by s -> s^(1/3) near 0, the local coordinate has difference quotients t^(-2/3) along the orbit of 0: the C^1 clause needs a C^1 flow.

layers.title: Bowen's uniqueness criterion under weak specification

targets.name: Flow.HasLowerGibbsProperty
targets.statement: mu in M(g) has the lower Gibbs property for phi at scale eps with constant K >= 1 when mu(B_t(x,eps)) exp(t P_g(phi) - int_0^t phi(g^s x) ds) >= K^{-1} for every x and t >= 0; Gibbs measures of maps are ClassicalErgodicTheory's IsGibbsMeasure (8.4).

api.name: lowerGibbs_of_large_times
api.statement: A bound for t >= T0 with constant K gives every t >= 0 with K e^{2 T0 (|P| + max|phi|)}, since B_t contains B_{T0} for t <= T0.

api.name: lowerGibbs_pos_open
api.statement: Lower Gibbs at arbitrarily small scales gives positive mass to nonempty open sets.

api.name: lowerGibbs_cohomologous
api.statement: Lower Gibbs for phi iff for phi + c (same K) and for phi + L_g psi (K times e^{2 sup|psi|}).

tests.name: periodic_orbit
tests.statement: Periodic orbit of period p: time measure, P the orbit average, B_t an arc of measure ~ eps/p: lower Gibbs.

tests.name: suspension_bernoulli
tests.statement: Roof-one suspension of the two-shift, phi = 0, product measure: mu(B_t) ~ eps 2^{-t-2m} for eps = 2^{-m}, times 2^t bounded below; the opposite sign gives ~ 4^{-t} -> 0.

tests.name: periodic_measure_nonexample
tests.statement: The time measure of a periodic orbit of that suspension is not lower Gibbs for phi = 0.

targets.name: Dynamics.existsUnique_isEquilibriumState_of_expansive_weakSpecification
targets.statement: X nonempty compact metric, T expansive homeomorphism (ClassicalErgodicTheory 5.3) with weak specification, phi continuous with HasBowenProperty: unique equilibrium state, ergodic, IsGibbsMeasure (Gibbs at every sufficiently small scale), positive on nonempty open sets; generalises ClassicalErgodicTheory 8.4's theorem (periodic specification implies weak specification).
hypotheses: phi continuous with the Bowen property

locator.where: Theorem 5.5, lines 1717-1724; Proposition 6.16, line 1955; Lemma 6.13, lines 1908-1910 (n >= N(M); smaller n by B_n containing B_{N(M)}); Proposition 6.17, lines 1963-1965; scales lines 1880-1887

tests.name: bernoulli
tests.statement: Full shift, phi(x_0): Bernoulli weights e^phi/sum.

tests.name: swap_ergodic_not_mixing
tests.statement: The swap satisfies the hypotheses but not ClassicalErgodicTheory's specification; ergodic, not mixing.

tests.name: union_nonexample
tests.statement: Two disjoint shifts: no weak specification, ES(0) a segment.

tests.name: small_n_lower_bound
tests.statement: Two-shift, phi = 0: a lower bound proved for n >= N gives n = 1 (mu(B_1(x,1/2)) = 1/8) with Q replaced by Q 2^{-2N}.

targets.name: Flow.existsUnique_isEquilibriumState_of_expansive_weakSpecification
targets.statement: X nonempty compact metric, g Bowen-Walters expansive flow (IsExpansiveFlow) with weak specification, phi continuous with HasFlowBowenProperty: unique flow equilibrium state, flow-ergodic, lower Gibbs property (5.1) at small scales, positive on nonempty open sets; generalises ClassicalErgodicTheory 8.5's theorem, covering the roof-one suspension of the two-shift.

locator.where: Theorem A, lines 140-147; Proposition 4.19, line 1489; Lemma 4.16, lines 1251-1253 (t >= T(M)); Proposition 4.15, lines 1243-1244

tests.name: suspension_nonmixing
tests.statement: Constant-roof suspension of the two-shift: unique MME, not mixing.

tests.name: periodic_orbit
tests.statement: Periodic orbit: time measure for every potential.

tests.name: identity_two_points
tests.statement: Identity flow of two points: no weak specification, every measure is an MME.

targets.name: Dynamics.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure
targets.statement: A homeomorphism of a compact metric space has hyperbolic local product structure if (A2) W^s_delta(x) meets W^u_delta(z) when d(x,z) < e(delta) and (A3) local stable/unstable sets contract exponentially forward/backward; Axiom A* adds (A1) dense periodic points.

api.name: bracket
api.statement: For 2 delta <= delta* and d(x,z) < e(delta) the intersection is a single point [x,z] (two such points stay 2 delta-close, so coincide by eq_of_forall_dist_le); continuous, [x,x] = x, f[x,z] = [fx,fz].

api.name: hlps_inv_iterate
api.statement: f^{-1} (s and u exchanged) and f^k (rate lambda^k) have the structure.

api.name: hlps_biLipschitz
api.statement: Invariant under bi-Lipschitz change of metric.

api.name: eq_of_forall_dist_le
api.statement: If d(f^n y, f^n y') <= delta* for all n in Z then y = y': f^n y' lies in W^u_{delta*}(f^n y), so d(y,y') <= c lambda^n delta* for all n >= 0 by (A3).

tests.name: full_shift
tests.statement: Full two-shift: W^s_{1/2}(x) = {y_i = x_i, i >= 0}, c = 1, lambda = 1/2, bracket by coordinates; Axiom A*.

tests.name: finite_identity
tests.statement: The identity of a finite set satisfies Axiom A*.

tests.name: rotation_nonexample
tests.statement: Irrational rotation and identity of the circle fail (A3).

targets.name: Dynamics.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure.expansive_shadowing_closing
targets.statement: Hyperbolic local product structure implies: expansive with constant delta* (from 6.1's coincidence lemma); shadowing of pseudo-orbits by points, unique when 2 beta <= delta*; closing lemma; transitive in forward time (for nonempty open U, V some n >= 0 has f^n U meeting V) implies dense periodic points (Axiom A*).
hypotheses: f homeomorphism with hyperbolic local product structure

locator.where: Lemma 2.3, lines 96-97; 2.5, lines 101-104; proof of 2.10, lines 171-200; Bowen1975 Chapter 3; KatokHasselblatt1995 Section 18.1

tests.name: shift_shadowing
tests.statement: On the full shift the shadowing point reads off zeroth symbols; closing repeats the first m symbols.

tests.name: finite_identity
tests.statement: Pseudo-orbits of the identity of a finite set are constant.

tests.name: rotation_nonexample
tests.statement: The irrational rotation has unshadowed pseudo-orbits and no periodic points.

tests.name: shift_large_beta
tests.statement: On the two-shift (diameter 1, delta* = 1/2) with beta = 1 every point shadows every pseudo-orbit; uniqueness needs 2 beta <= delta*.

tests.name: monotone_shift_signed_time
tests.statement: The monotone shift {x in {0,1}^Z : x_i <= x_(i+1)} has hyperbolic local product structure (c = 1, lambda = 1/2) and a dense Z-orbit, but its only periodic points are 0^Z and 1^Z; it is not transitive in forward time (T^n{x_0 = 1} stays in {x_0 = 1} for n >= 0), so the last item needs the forward notion.

targets.name: Dynamics.AxiomAStar.spectralDecomposition_specification
targets.statement: Axiom A*: spectral decomposition into cyclically permuted closed pieces with C-dense return maps; strong specification for C-dense f; transitive f has weak specification at every scale and h_top > 0 unless X is finite.

tests.name: swap_two_pieces
tests.statement: The swap has two pieces fixed by f^2; weak not strong specification.

tests.name: shift_one_piece
tests.statement: The full shift is C-dense with one piece.

tests.name: union_nonexample
tests.statement: Two disjoint shifts: permutation not a cycle, not transitive.

targets.name: Dynamics.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure.hasBowenProperty_of_holder
targets.statement: With hyperbolic local product structure, every Hoelder potential has the Bowen property, with K = 2C(c delta)^theta/(1 - lambda^theta).
hypotheses: f with hyperbolic local product structure

tests.name: coordinate_lipschitz
tests.statement: x -> x_0 on the two-shift is Lipschitz and Bowen with K = 0.

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: Constants are Hoelder and Bowen with K = 0.

tests.name: harmonic_not_holder
tests.statement: phi(x) = 1/m, m the least i >= 1 with x_i = 1: for every m', the point with its only 1 at n + m' stays 2^(-m')-close to 0 for n steps with Birkhoff sums differing by 1/(m'+1) + ... + 1/(n+m'), so it is Bowen at no scale, and it is not Hoelder.

targets.name: Flow.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure
targets.statement: A continuous flow without fixed points on a compact metric space has hyperbolic local product structure if (F2) nearby x, z have a unique small v with W^s_delta(g^v x) meeting W^u_delta(z) and (F3) strong stable/unstable sets contract exponentially.
hypotheses: g continuous flow without fixed points

locator.where: lines 96-108 for the stable and unstable sets; (F2), (F3) are this roadmap's flow analogue of BowenPeriodicPoints1971 (A2), (A3), lines 74-80, verified in 8.5; FH2019 Part II

api.name: flow_bracket
api.statement: Bracket [x,z] and time shift v continuous, equivariant.

api.name: flow_hlps_reverse
api.statement: Reversal exchanges W^s, W^u; rescaling multiplies kappa.

api.name: weak_stable_transversal
api.statement: Nearby z lies in W^u_delta of the point [x,z] of W^cs_delta(x).

tests.name: suspension
tests.statement: Constant-roof suspension of the two-shift: bracket at matched heights, v the height difference.

tests.name: periodic_orbit
tests.statement: On a periodic orbit W^s and W^u are points and z = g^v x.

tests.name: linear_nonexample
tests.statement: The irrational linear flow satisfies (F3) vacuously (both strong sets are {x}) but fails (F2): a nearby point off the orbit segment meets no W^s_delta(g^v x).

targets.name: Flow.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure.expansive_closing_specification
targets.statement: Hyperbolic local product structure implies Bowen-Walters expansivity and closing; flows transitive in forward time (for nonempty open U, V some t >= 0 has g^t U meeting V) have dense periodic orbits and weak specification at every scale.
hypotheses: g with hyperbolic local product structure

locator.where: Example 1.6*, lines 134-135; BowenWalters1972; FH2019 Part II; KatokHasselblatt1995 Section 18.1

tests.name: suspension_weak_spec
tests.statement: The suspension has weak specification with gaps in [0, tau0 + 1] but integer periods.

tests.name: periodic_orbit
tests.statement: Periodic orbit: dense periodic orbit, gaps at most one period.

tests.name: two_orbits_nonexample
tests.statement: Two disjoint periodic orbits: not transitive, no weak specification.

tests.name: monotone_suspension_signed_time
tests.statement: The roof-one suspension of the monotone shift has hyperbolic local product structure and a dense orbit, but only two periodic orbits and no weak specification: flow boxes over {x_0 = 1} never meet flow boxes over {x_0 = 0} at times t >= 0.

targets.name: Flow.HasHyperbolicLocalProductStructure.hasBowenProperty_of_holder
targets.statement: With hyperbolic local product structure, every Hoelder potential has the Bowen property for the flow: for eps <= e(delta), y in B_t(x,eps), the time shift satisfies |v| <= delta, the shift error is at most 2 delta max|phi| and the stable and unstable legs are geometric integrals; no bound of |v| by a multiple of d(x,y) is used.
hypotheses: g with hyperbolic local product structure

locator.where: Appendix, Lemma A.2, lines 681-701; ClimenhagaThompson2016 lines 341-342

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: Constants are Bowen with K = 0.

tests.name: suspension_potential
tests.statement: A potential of the zeroth symbol, Lipschitz in height, is Bowen on the suspension.

tests.name: coboundary_independent
tests.statement: For a C^1 flow on a manifold, L_g psi of a C^1 psi has orbit integrals psi o g^t - psi, so HasFlowBowenProperty with K = 4 sup|psi|, without hyperbolicity.

tests.name: cubic_time_shift
tests.statement: Circle flow conjugate to the rotation by s -> s^3 near 0: (F2), (F3) hold with singleton strong sets and d(0, g^v 0) = |v|^3, so |v| is not O(d), while |v| <= delta holds.

targets.name: Dynamics.existsUnique_isEquilibriumState_of_hyperbolic
targets.statement: With transitivity in forward time: (a) transitive homeomorphism with hyperbolic local product structure and Hoelder phi: unique, ergodic, Gibbs, fully supported equilibrium state; unique MME, h_top > 0 unless X finite. (b) same for transitive flows with flow-ergodicity and lower Gibbs bound.
hypotheses: f or g transitive in forward time (n >= 0, resp. t >= 0) with hyperbolic local product structure

locator.where: 8.1, lines 749-750; Remark 4.4, lines 421-426; ClimenhagaThompson2016 Theorem 5.5 and Theorem A

tests.name: bernoulli
tests.statement: Full shift, phi(x_0): the Bernoulli measure of 5.2.

tests.name: swap_finite
tests.statement: The swap: h_top = 0, unique measure.

tests.name: periodic_orbit_flow
tests.statement: Periodic orbit: time measure, entropy 0.

tests.name: monotone_shift_two_states
tests.statement: The monotone shift (transitive only in signed time) has h_top = 0 and M(T) the segment between the point masses at 0^Z and 1^Z, all equilibrium states of phi = 0; its roof-one suspension has two periodic-orbit equilibrium states of F = 0.

layers.title: Hyperbolic sets and their linear theory

targets.name: Manifold.IsHyperbolicSet
targets.statement: Compact Lambda with f(Lambda) = Lambda is hyperbolic for a C^1 diffeomorphism and a continuous Riemannian metric if there are C > 0, 0 < lambda < 1 and invariant complementary E^s_x, E^u_x with |Df^n v| <= C lambda^n |v| on E^s and |Df^{-n} v| <= C lambda^n |v| on E^u; f is Anosov if M is compact and hyperbolic.
hypotheses: M finite-dimensional smooth manifold without boundary
f : Diffeomorph I I M M 1

locator.where: Part I, Section 1.3, lines 381-473; KatokHasselblatt1995 Section 6.4

api.name: isHyperbolicSet_subset
api.statement: A closed subset with f(Lambda') = Lambda' of a hyperbolic set is hyperbolic with the restricted splitting; finite unions are in 7.4.

api.name: isHyperbolicSet_fixedPoint_iff
api.statement: {p} is hyperbolic iff Df_p has no eigenvalue of modulus 1.

api.name: isHyperbolicSet_conj
api.statement: Invariant under C^1 conjugacy.

tests.name: diag_saddle
tests.statement: {0} is hyperbolic for diag(2,1/2) with E^s the second axis, C = 1, lambda = 1/2; not for diag(2,1).

tests.name: identity_nonexample

layers.title: Basic sets and the Bowen-Ruelle theorem

targets.name: Manifold.IsBasicSet
targets.statement: A basic set is a nonempty locally maximal hyperbolic set on which the diffeomorphism or flow is transitive in forward time (some n >= 0, resp. t >= 0, has f^n U, resp. g^t U, meeting V); an attractor is a basic set with a neighbourhood U, g^t U in U for t >= T0, Lambda = intersection of g^t U; its basin is the set of points asymptotic to Lambda. For x in Lambda, W^s_x(eps) = {y in M : d(g^t y, g^t x) <= eps for t >= 0, -> 0} and W^s_Lambda(eps) is their union; for an attractor of a C^1 flow and small eps it contains the closed alpha-neighbourhood of Lambda and the basin is the union of the g^{-t}(W^s_Lambda(eps)).
hypotheses: f C^1 diffeomorphism or g C^1 flow

locator.where: lines 25-34 and 94-95 (dense orbit plus dense periodic orbits); lines 381-383 and 402-406 for W^s_Lambda(eps), citing HirschPalisPughShub1970 Section 5.1

api.name: basicSet_periodic_dense
api.statement: Periodic points are dense in a basic set.

api.name: basicSet_of_signed_transitive_periodic_dense
api.statement: A nonempty locally maximal hyperbolic set, transitive in signed time with dense periodic points (orbits), is a basic set; with the periodic density API, basic sets are exactly Bowen-Ruelle's basic hyperbolic sets.

api.name: anosov_basicSet
api.statement: A transitive Anosov system on a nonempty compact manifold is a basic set Lambda = M and an attractor with basin M.

api.name: basicSet_inv

Route: strong unstable plaques of points of Lambda lie in Lambda; weak stable plaques over the unstable plaque fill a neighbourhood by TauCeti.brouwerFixedPoint_closedBall; 8.3's contraction.

targets.name: Manifold.grassmannBundle
targets.statement: (i) The Grassmann bundle G_q(TM) of q-planes in TM (GeometricCurrents G6's topological bundle), 0 <= q <= dim M, is a smooth manifold of dimension dim M + q(dim M - q), compact when M is, with charts from charts of M and graph coordinates (GeneralizedCohomology G4.0b, TauCeti.finiteGrassmannian.graphChart), transition (C + DL)(A + BL)^{-1}. (ii) For a flow with C^2 generator, G_q g^t(x,E) = (g^t x, Dg^t_x E) is a C^1 flow with C^1 generator covering X, and Phi(x,E) = -d/dt log Jac(Dg^t|E) at 0 is C^1 with orbit integrals -log Jac(Dg^T|E). (iii) If dim E^u = q on a hyperbolic set Lambda, Lambda* = {E^u_x} is a hyperbolic set of G_q g with stable dimension dim E^s + q(dim M - q) and unstable dimension q.
hypotheses: M compact smooth manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric
g a flow with C^2 generator
Lambda hyperbolic with dim E^u = q (for (iii))

tests.name: extreme_q
tests.statement: q = 0 or q = dim M: fibres are points, G_q(TM) is a copy of M, dimension dim M.

tests.name: stable_lift_nonexample
tests.statement: The lift of E^s is invariant but its fibre directions expand (unstable dimension 3, not 1).

tests.name: c1_generator
tests.statement: With a C^1 generator G_q g is only continuous and Phi only continuous: the C^2 hypothesis is needed.

targets.name: Flow.IsHyperbolicSet.boundedDistortion
targets.statement: (a) For a hyperbolic set of any C^1 flow on a compact manifold with a smooth metric (Lambda for g, or Lambda* of 11.2 for G_q g), C^1 psi and theta > 0 there is delta: |int_0^T psi(g^t y) - int_0^T psi(g^t x)| < theta for x in the hyperbolic set, y in the manifold, T >= 0, d(g^t y, g^t x) < delta on [0,T] (BowenRuelle1975 A.2, r = 1). (b) For theta > 0 there are delta, eta > 0: if moreover E* in T_yM has dim E^u_x and every Dg^t E*, t in [0,T], read in the chart at g^t x is the graph of a linear map E^u -> E^s + RX of norm < eta, then e^{-theta} <= Jac(Dg^T|E*)/lambda_T(x) <= e^theta, by (a) for Lambda* and the function Phi of 11.2. (c) Tangent planes to the chart slices phi_x(v + E^u_x(eps)) along chart orbits staying in eps-balls up to integer time n satisfy (b) (BowenRuelle1975 A.4).
hypotheses: g C^2 flow with C^2 generator, smooth metric
T >= 0; plane tolerance eta depending on theta

locator.where: Appendix, Lemma A.2, lines 681-701; Lemma A.3, lines 702-715; Lemma A.4, lines 718-739; chart estimates lines 655-676

tests.name: linear_flow
tests.statement: Suspension of the cat map, x = y, E* spanned by e_u + b e_v: the ratio is (1 + b^2 e^{-4aT})^(1/2)/(1 + b^2)^(1/2), tending to (1+b^2)^(-1/2); for b = 0.1 the limit 0.99504 < e^-0.001, so eta must depend on theta (b^2 <= e^{2 theta} - 1 is exactly what is needed).

tests.name: bowen_property_case
tests.statement: For E* = E^u_y this is the Bowen property of phi^u.

tests.name: c1_nonexample
tests.statement: Without C^2 the ratio can be unbounded.

targets.name: Flow.IsHyperbolicSet.volumeLemma
targets.statement: (a) c_eps^{-1} <= m(B_x(eps,T)) lambda_T(x) <= c_eps for x in Lambda, T > 0; (b) m(B_y(delta,T)) >= d m(B_x(eps,T)) for y in B_x(eps,T); m the Riemannian volume.
hypotheses: g C^2 flow on compact M with C^2 generator
m = riemannianVolume of the smooth metric

targets.name: Flow.IsBasicSet.pressure_geometricPotential
targets.statement: (a) P(g|Lambda, phi^u) = limsup (1/T) log m(B_Lambda(eps,T)) <= 0; (b) if W^s_Lambda(eps) of 10.1 has positive volume (attractors, Anosov), P = 0 and h_{mu+}(g^1) = -integral phi^u d mu+, since B_Lambda(eps,T) contains W^s_Lambda(eps).
hypotheses: g C^2 flow on compact M with C^2 generator, smooth metric
Lambda basic set (nonempty); Anosov case on a nonempty compact manifold

tests.name: saddle_orbit
tests.statement: A saddle periodic orbit has P(phi^u) = -(1/p) log lambda_p < 0.

tests.name: covering_radius_attracting_circle
tests.statement: Attracting periodic orbit r = 0 of theta' = 1, r' = -sin(2 pi r)/(2 pi) on the flat torus, delta = 1/(3.9m), eps = 1.01 delta, centres j/m: the maximal disjoint-ball family misses y = (1/(2m), eps) at radius delta + eps = 2.01 delta (distance 2.196 delta) but covers it at 2 delta + eps.

targets.name: Flow.IsBasicSet.srb
targets.statement: For an attractor of g, m-almost every point of the basin is generic for mu+ = nu_{g,phi^u}; for transitive Anosov g on a nonempty compact manifold mu+ is the unique invariant probability whose generic points have positive (full) volume, and every g-invariant probability absolutely continuous with respect to m equals mu+. No absolute continuity of mu+ is asserted, and no absolutely continuous invariant probability need exist.
hypotheses: g C^2 flow on compact M with C^2 generator, smooth metric
Lambda attractor (a nonempty basic set) with basin W^s_Lambda

tests.name: hyperbolic_surface
tests.statement: Curvature -1 surface: Bowen-Margulis = SRB = Liouville.

tests.name: cat_suspension_volume
tests.statement: Suspension of the cat map: mu+ is the product measure, the normalised volume for the metric of 11.1; after the conformal factor e^{2u(s)}, u = 0.1 sin(2 pi s), the volume has density proportional to e^{3u(s)}, not invariant, in the measure class of mu+.

tests.name: uniqueness_generic
tests.statement: Two measures with positive-volume generic sets coincide.

tests.name: covering_radius_3eps
tests.statement: Attracting circle of 10.1, z = (0,0), x = (2 eps, 0), y = (0, eps) in W^s_z(eps): the closed eps-discs about z and x (the Bowen balls) meet at (eps, 0) but d(y, x) = sqrt5 eps > 2 eps, and <= 3 eps.

gaps.title: Smooth corestriction into the unit sphere bundle
gaps.detail: Tau Ceti supplies the unit sphere bundle with its regular-level atlas (TauCeti.sphereBundleChartedSpace), its manifold structure (TauCeti.isManifold_sphereBundle) and the smooth embedding of its inclusion (TauCeti.isSmoothEmbedding_coe_sphereBundle). The geodesic-flow example needs the restricted flow, a smooth map into the total space with values in the sphere bundle, to be smooth into the sphere bundle; no corestriction theorem for this atlas was found at the pins.
gaps.needs: For the unit sphere bundle of a C^n Riemannian vector bundle with Tau Ceti's regular-level atlas, a C^n map from a C^n manifold into the total space with values in the sphere bundle is C^n into the sphere bundle.

gaps.title: Connection map and the Jacobi-field derivative of the geodesic flow
gaps.detail: RiemannianGeometry R2 supplies Jacobi fields and variations through geodesics but not the connection map of the Levi-Civita connection, the horizontal-vertical splitting of T(TM), or the identification of the derivative of the geodesic flow with the Jacobi-field map; proposed as RiemannianGeometry, Part II.
gaps.needs: For a smooth Riemannian manifold with its Levi-Civita connection: the connection map K : T(TM) -> TM, the horizontal-vertical splitting of T_v(TM) identified with T_x M + T_x M, and, for v in TM, xi in T_v(TM) with components (w, w') and t in the domain of the geodesic of v, D(geodesic flow at time t)_v xi = (J(t), D_t J(t)) where J is the Jacobi field along that geodesic with J(0) = w, D_t J(0) = w'.
gaps.section: proposed Part II: connection map and Jacobi derivative of the geodesic flow
